call_order.claim: Cell initialization resets state, initializes pool support, loads world/UI/serializable references, and invokes stage rebuild/setup before returning
Cell object creation computes content/size state, obtains a pool slot, initializes object fields, creates query/effect/GFX associations, and returns the index
Cell despawn detaches avatar/query/GFX/association state, may create a replacement, and releases the old object
Star regeneration writes observation time and pending/manager state before calling the planet-generation body
order: erase pending star and reset manager state

call_order.claim: Star persistence follows generation/availability work and uses temporary database state before persistent replacement

lifecycle_limits: No positive runtime trace is available for Cell spawn, death, despawn, stage rebuild, city vehicle spawn, tribe population, herd respawn, or star regeneration.

The original generic cObjectPool_ address mapping is contradictory near 0x00b72160/0x00b72260/0x00b72270, so generic pool behavior is not treated as universally interchangeable with the Cell-specific pool.
The current OpenSpore CellPool is a clean-room projection; it is evidence for tests and structure preservation, not proof of original runtime population semantics.
All population-cap names from SDK fields are treated as state surfaces until their comparison and mutation bodies are recovered.

ownership.fact: cCellGame owns the main cell pool, current/background query handles, current/background world references, and mAvatarCellIndex
Each cCellObjectData first word carries pool identity/free-list linkage; object-specific GFX/query/association cleanup precedes pool reuse for the recovered despawn path
cStarManager owns the star grid and temporary/persistent planet-record database handles; cStarRecord carries the count and lazy planet vector
SDK intrusive vectors indicate member/plan/city population ownership surfaces, but exact runtime add/remove and release ordering are not recovered
